One advantage to having multiple bikes that I never see discussed is the ability to change from one to another to minimize injuries due to repeated stress. When my ass gets sore from one bike seat, I ride a different bike seat. When my knees hurt from a long ride on my flatbar road bike, I switch to my hybrid. Because I switch around, I don't really get persistent aches and pains.

I know what you're going to say -- if I had a professional bike fitting, I wouldn't have these problems in the first place. I don't believe that. Even with a perfectly fitted bike, the stress on your body is always going to be in the same places, and some of those places are going to complain. By shifting around from bike to bike, I move the stress around on my body, and give body parts that start to ache time to recover. It works for me.
